turns.prompt_text: How old is the field of computer science?
turns.response_html:
The age of computer science depends on how you define the field. As an official, standalone academic discipline, it is roughly 60 to 65 years old. However, if you look at the theoretical foundations of computing, the field is nearly a century old—and its earliest precursors date back well into the 19th century.

Here is how the field evolved from a mathematical concept into its own distinct discipline:

Prior to the 1960s, people who worked on computers were typically mathematicians, physicists, or electrical engineers. It was only when hardware became complex enough to require dedicated software and operating systems that computer science officially broke away to become the field we recognize today.
